chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: J. J. Johnson as idol and friend
summary: Baker describes J. J. Johnson as his idol on trombone, a close friend and one of the last surviving bebop pioneers.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: J. J. Johnson: the boss. Jay, my idol on the trombone, and, since I’ve been an adult, one of my very closest friends and confidants, and somebody that I think is one of the original voices in the music, one of the survivors. There are only maybe five or six of the bebop pioneers left: J. J., [James] Moody, Ray Brown, Max Roach. I’m hard pressed to figure out who else. But J. J.: survivor, innovator, mentor, and friend.
